text: Today's icon works, but both band edges pass behind the mark: one cuts across the notch, and at 16 px the band breaks into pieces either side of the bookmark.
Curved bands from the bottom-right corner leave one loud sweep across the middle and ground under the bar. Two colours only, so it held up in five palettes, and reads at 16 px.
Today's icon and the best of the bands: nearly three quarters of the mark sits on one loud sweep, with ground only at the bottom right and the top-left rim. Reads at 16 px.
One curve from the top left puts the mark's lower half on one colour, but a hairline crescent at the bottom-right rim shows as a fleck in the corner at small sizes.
Today's bands turned half a turn, so the patch of ground moves from under the bar to behind the bookmark's top-left shoulder. Just as strong if the patch should sit high.
The hill's crest hides behind the bookmark and its edge comes out at the bookmark's lower sides, so the notch and the whole bar sit on one colour; two calm bands at 16 and 32 px.
A dome rising from the bottom edge shows either side of the bookmark, so the mark stands on a horizon. Symmetric, two colours, and the cleanest of the set at 16 and 32 px.
The best half-disc pattern: the bar stands on a loud dome and the bookmark's top on plain ground. The least busy of any pick, with the cleanest two-colour read at 16 px.
The Hill with a mid-tone sky, so on light grounds the bookmark never stands on a colour close to paper. On dark grounds the line between sky and hill is softer at 16 px.
The Hill with its sky in a supporting colour, so it reads as a small landscape on light grounds. On dark grounds sky and hill are closer in tone.
The cap's curve hides behind the bookmark, leaving the notch, the gap above the bar and the bar on one plain colour; at 16 px the cap is about a pixel tall.
The Hill's dome hung from the top edge: a loud cap over the bookmark, just as clean at small sizes, though the mark then stands on nothing.
Two big side-by-side fields read cleanly at 16 and 32 px, but the curve passes through the centre: it splits the notch and comes out under the bar, so colours meet at the bookmark's tip.
A half disc from the right edge splits the circle along a curve just behind the mark, so the icon reads as two side-by-side fields, which looks lopsided under an upright mark.
The ring frames the mark like a porthole, but its inner disc is barely bigger than the mark: the bookmark's top corners touch its edge and the bar's ends cross it.
A loud ring round a plain disc makes a calm, symmetric halo behind the mark in every palette, though a circle in a round mask looks more like a frame than a cover.
The plain centre backs the whole mark, a badge at 16 px, but the bookmark hides the ring's top, leaving a border; on a light ground the mark leans on its outline.
A straight line runs from the bookmark's top-right shoulder to the bar's left end, its one awkward crossing. The notch and the rest of the bar sit on loud colour: the boldest at 16 px.
Lines of ground part a big half circle on the right from two small discs on the left, a two-colour figure that held up in every palette. At 16 px the lines turn to specks.
Two colours, mirrored top to bottom: a curved strip of ground runs down behind the mark like a book's spine. Very calm, but at 16 px the strip hides and it nearly flattens.
A loud field with one disc in a supporting colour at the top right, like a moon behind the bookmark: one clear accent, though deliberately off-centre.
One loud field backs about two thirds of the mark, with a single bite at the top right, a disc on ground that reads as a crescent: one accent, one flat backing.
Three loud curved shapes and one in a supporting colour bite in from the corners, leaving the ground as a four-pointed star around the mark. One clear figure, but busy at 16 px.
The best of the four-pointed stars: a star of ground between curved corner shapes, with the mark at its centre. Five changes of colour around the mark make it noisy at 16 px.
Top and bottom halves meet along an S-shaped wave, lovely without the mark, but the wave crosses the centre and hides behind the mark, leaving a plain top-and-bottom split.
An S-shaped horizon: the calmest four-shape pattern and the strongest at 16 px on a light ground. On a dark ground the lower half turns pale, so a paper bar would vanish there.
Curved quarter and half discs form a yin-yang S across all four colours, distinctive without the mark, but the S sits in the centre, where the bookmark covers it.
A loud curve on the left meets a cap of a supporting colour at the top right, the other two colours below: the most fluid four-colour pattern, but all four meet around the mark.
A band in a supporting colour crosses behind the bookmark's lower half, and 89% of the mark sits on plain loud colour: the clearest backing of any four-shape pattern. Still reads at 16 px.
A loud field with one cut-away corner at the top right, beside the bookmark, like a dog-eared page, which suits a reading app, but that corner is three slivers that go fussy at 16 px.
Four plain quarters, loud in two opposite corners, with a disc in the top-right quarter. The plainest four-shape pattern: the mark sits on two colours with a clear cross around it.
The opposite of Moon: nearly all plain ground, with a loud curve in the top-right corner. Elegant and still on dark grounds; pale on light ones, where the mark relies on its outline.
A hard vertical split: one colour fills the right half, two share the left. Boldest at 16 px on a light ground, but on dark grounds the right half turns pale behind half the mark.
